review_notes: I read the whole target file and grepped the sibling Determinantal files for the definitions the file uses: edgeExponent, baseEdges, expandedWeight, gadgetH and allOnes. I did not run Lean, so I don't claim that any proposed lemma compiles or that any simp set behaves a given way. The existing @[simp] set for selectorSplit (C, main, gate) looks coherent: the left-hand sides are distinct constructors, and I found no rewrite loop. The findings are about missing canonical simp lemmas. Each one is currently replaced by repeated local `have`s or by unfolding definitions inside `simp [...]` calls. I did not report rename_inner/rename_outer or allOnes_block, because the evidence for them was weaker.

findings.excerpt:
have hm (i j : SelectorOuter I h) (r : R) : monomial (edgeExponent (i,j)) r =
      C r * X (.inl i) * X (.inr j) := by
findings.problem: The canonical rewrite `monomial (edgeExponent (i,j)) r = C r * X (.inl i) * X (.inr j)` has no named simp lemma. This file proves it as `hm`, then proves the same statement again as `hx` for `M i j` (lines 113-116). Selector.lean (lines 271 and 330) and Gates.lean (line 163) each prove it again. Each time it is a local `have` that is fed to `simp only`, so the normal form for edge monomials is not part of the simp interface.
findings.proposed_change: Next to `edgeExponent` in Selector.lean, add one lemma `monomial_edgeExponent (i j : n) (r : R) : monomial (edgeExponent (i,j)) r = C r * X (.inl i) * X (.inr j)` and mark it @[simp]. It has no side conditions and is oriented toward the form that map_mul and rename/split lemmas consume. Then delete `hm` and `hx` here and in the other proofs. The `simp only [baseEdges, hm, ...]` call and the `edgeProduct` branch can then use the lemma directly, and `hx` plus the `rw [hx, map_mul, map_mul]` step become redundant.
findings.benefit: One lemma replaces five copies of the same proof, and the `edgeExponent`-monomial form is rewritten consistently across the Determinantal files. Later proofs about base edges no longer need a local bridge lemma.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def selectorWeight (θ : I → R) (g : Fin 2 × I) : R :=
  if g.1=0 then 1 else θ g.2
findings.problem: `selectorWeight` is an `if` on the `Fin 2` coordinate, but it has no simp equations for the two cases that occur: `selectorWeight θ (0,i) = 1` and `selectorWeight θ (1,i) = θ i`. Downstream proofs unfold it instead. `h0` and `h1` in `selector_boundary_coeff` use `simp [selectorBoundaryWeight, selectorWeight]` (lines 175-178). `selectorMatrix_map` unfolds it and then needs `split_ifs` (line 284). `selectorBoundaryWeight` has the same gap. Unfolding exposes `if (1:Fin 2) = 0` conditions, which then have to be decided every time.
findings.proposed_change: Add @[simp] lemmas `selectorWeight_zero : selectorWeight θ (0,i) = 1` and `selectorWeight_one : selectorWeight θ (1,i) = θ i`. Add `selectorBoundaryWeight_zero : selectorBoundaryWeight θ 0 i = X (.inl i) * X (.inr i)` and `selectorBoundaryWeight_one : selectorBoundaryWeight θ 1 i = C (θ i) * X (.inl i) * X (.inr i)`, with the second also marked @[simp] or used via `simp only`. Then `h0` and `h1` reduce to `funext i; simp` or disappear, and the unfolding in `selectorMatrix_map` can stop at the lemmas. Keep the definitions semireducible rather than unfolding them in call sites.
findings.benefit: The two cases are stated once as readable rewrite rules. Proofs stop depending on the `if` implementation and no longer unfold the definition, and the `Fin 2` case split is handled by lemmas rather than `simp` arithmetic on `Fin` literals.

findings.excerpt:
theorem gadgetH_map (f : R →+* S) (r c : Fin 3) :
    f (gadgetH (R := R) r c) = gadgetH r c := by
findings.problem: This is the standard map-compatibility lemma for the constant matrix `gadgetH`. It is not tagged @[simp], so its sole use passes it by hand to `simp_all [gadgetH_map, map_ofNat]` (line 285). `gadgetH` entries are integer literals (`!![-1,-1,1; ...]`). Ring homomorphisms commute with them, as with `map_natCast` and `map_ofNat`. Any other proof that maps a gate expansion through a ring hom has to re-supply the lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it @[simp] and move it next to the `gadgetH` definition in Selector.lean, where it applies to every user of `expandedWeight`. Its left-hand side `f (gadgetH r c)` is headed by a ring hom applied to `gadgetH`, and its right-hand side has strictly less structure, so I see no loop. The call at line 285 then no longer needs to name it.
findings.benefit: Ring-hom maps through `expandedWeight` and `expandedMatrix` simplify without the user having to know this auxiliary lemma. The canonical form of `f (gadgetH r c)` is `gadgetH r c`.

findings.problem: `selectorLinearEntries` is defined by a catch-all match, and it is the key term in the affine decomposition. It has no simp equations: no `selectorLinearEntries M h (.inl (.inl i)) (.inl (.inl j)) = M i j` and no zero cases. Every consumer therefore unfolds the definition and manually does a three-by-three `rcases` on both indices (lines 263-264 and 296-297), with the unfolding handled by `simp [selectorLinearEntries, ...]`. The catch-all match also leaves overlapping equation lemmas, which are awkward in `simp` when the indices are not literal constructors.
findings.proposed_change: Add @[simp] lemmas: `selectorLinearEntries_main (M i j) : selectorLinearEntries M h (.inl (.inl i)) (.inl (.inl j)) = M i j`. Add `selectorLinearEntries_zero_of_gate`, i.e. `selectorLinearEntries M h (.inr g) c = 0` and `selectorLinearEntries M h r (.inr g) = 0`, together with the `.inl (.inr _)` variants. Also add `selectorLinearEntries_zero : selectorLinearEntries 0 h r c = 0`. This lets `selectorMatrix_affine` and `selectorLinearEntries_sum` use `simp` after the case split without unfolding the definition. Because `selectorMatrix_affine` is stated for `selectorMatrix 0 θ h`, the last lemma also makes the `M = 0` instance used in `selector_polynomial_affine` simplify directly.
findings.benefit: The constructor-by-constructor behaviour is explicit in the simp set, so a change to `SelectorVertex` or to the definition doesn't need the case analysis redone in every proof that touches the linear part.
